paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Yunnan, the tea English calls black. The Chinese name follows the red of the brewed cup. Red tea made in this province from the large leaf of its own tea trees is known as [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition). The garden this leaf came from was not recorded.

Dian Hong began when the war cut China off from its eastern tea regions, the country needed a new red tea to sell abroad, and the national tea company turned to Yunnan. Feng Shaoqiu made [a trial batch in Shunning](dian-hong:history), now Fengqing, in late 1938, and a factory followed there the next year. For decades nearly all of it went overseas. It was sold widely in China only from the 1980s.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
